## Union Cabinet
race exposes AP
BJP faultlines

DC CORRESPONDENT
VIJAYAWADA, JUNE 11

Infighting among the old-
timers and leaders who
parachuted from other
parties, which has been
plaguing the Telangana
BJP, seems to have spread
to the party in neighbour-
ing Andhra Pradesh as
well.

With an expansion of the
Union Cabinet on the
cards, leaders like D.
Purandeshwari and C.M.
Ramesh have intensified
lobbying for a berth,
though old-timers pitched
for the continuation of
incumbent Bhoopathiraju
Srinivasa Varma.

Sources said the Central
leadership entrusting
Ramesh, the Anakapalle
MP, with the task of man-
aging the switchover of
Trinamul Congress Lok
Sabha members to the
BJP fold had upped his
stakes within the party.
They also claimed that it
was Ramesh who
arranged a meeting of
Trinamul rebel MPs with
senior BJP leader
Bhupender Yadav and
West Bengal Chief
Minister Suvendu
Adhikari at the latter's
residence a few days ago,
where things were firmed
up. "He then left for
Kolkata again to monitor
the task," said a BJP

leader close to Ramesh.
Prior to that, Ramesh
had been making round
trips to Delhi and Kolkata
in the past few weeks to
initiate dialogue with
rebel TMC MPs. “He is
being made part of the
deliberations at the high-
est level and arranging
the paraphernalia for
smooth completion of the
task,” a party leader told
Deccan Chronicle.

Purandeshwari, BJP MP
and former Union minis-
ter, has emerged as anoth-
er contender. Sources said
that since the party's
expansion plans were on
hold in Andhra Pradesh,
the Central leadership
would not allow a Cabinet
berth to go waste; besides,
she could not be demoted
to a minister of state.

Though she was made
AP unit president before
the 2024 elections, the BJP
central leadership
replaced Purandeshwari
with P.N.V. Madhav. On
the other hand, Srinivasa
Varma, a non-controver-
sial leader, is banking on
his staunch loyalty to the
party for his retention in
the Union ministry.
Senior leaders were
unhappy over actions of
some leaders parachuted
from other parties creat-
ing an impression that
money power matters in
the party.

## Another mishap in
Vizag steel plant



*ఈ చిత్రంలో ప్రధానమంత్రి నరేంద్ర మోదీ (Narendra Modi) ఒక సభలో ప్రసంగిస్తున్నారు. ఆయన తెల్లటి చొక్కా మరియు బూడిద రంగు జాకెట్ ధరించి, గంభీరంగా మాట్లాడుతున్నారు. ఆయన ముందు మైక్రోఫోన్లు మరియు నీటి సీసాలు ఉన్నాయి. ఆయన వెనుక ఇతర ప్రముఖులు కూర్చుని ఉన్నారు.*

K.M.P. PATNAIK | DC
VISAKHAPATNAM, JUNE 11

Another mishap took
place at the Steel Melting
Shop-1 of Visakhapatnam
Steel Plant (VSP) in the
early hours of Thursday,
jolting the employees who
were yet to recover from
the shock of Monday's
blast that killed nine
workers and injured five

others. Joint chief inspec-
tor of factories Siva
Sankar Reddy said that a
leak occurred in the ladle,
and molten steel erupted
onto the floor. “We took
the issue seriously and
told the management that
such incidents should be
avoided,” Siva Sankar
said.

## Stresses on women, youth, trade deals for achieving Viksit Bharat goals

MADHUSUDAN
SAHOO | DC
NEW DELHI, JUNE 11

Prime Minister Narendra
Modi on Thursday said
that India continues to
advance on its growth tra-
jectory with confidence
and determination despite
uncertainty and instability
across the world.

Stressing the need for the
Centre's and states' collec-
tive efforts for achieving
the Viksit Bharat goals,
the Prime Minister called
the youth, women and free-
trade agreements with
other nations the key dri-
vers of economic growth in
the country.

Chairing the 11th govern-
ing council meeting of Niti
Aayog at Rashtrapati
Bhavan in New Delhi,
Modi said that priority
should be given to the
MSMEs, start-ups, educa-
tion, skilling, safety and
empowerment of women to
unlock their full potential
and drive India’s develop-
ment journey.

“As India progresses
towards achieving the
vision of Viksit Bharat, the
collective responsibility of
the Centre and states

becomes even greater,”
Modi said.

The Prime Minister also
urged the creation of the
right ecosystem in the
country, saying that coop-
eration, dialogue and shar-
ing should guide interac-
tions among the states.

During the Niti Aayog
governing council discus-
sion, Modi mostly focused
on women and youth of the
country. “Women-led
development is a corner-
stone of the vision of Viksit
Bharat. From farming and
startups to science and
innovation, nari shakti is
contributing across the
domains,” he said

“Niti Aayog can play an
important role as a plat-
form for collaboration,
enabling states to
exchange ideas and work
together towards the
vision of Viksit Bharat,”

he said.

## Schools to reopen today
with festive atmosphere

## Kurnool top in enrolment; max schools in Srikakulam

RAMACHANDRA REDDY
GUNDAM | DC
KURNOOL, JUNE 11



*ఈ చిత్రంలో ఐదు రంగుల వృత్తాలు ఉన్నాయి. ఎడమ నుండి కుడికి: సియాన్, మెజెంటా, పసుపు, నలుపు, మరియు బూడిద రంగు.*

With schools set to
reopen from Friday, June
12, a festive atmosphere
is sweeping across
Andhra Pradesh. Parents
and students are gearing
up for the new academic
year with enthusiasm
and anticipation.

Parents are busy pur-
chasing essentials, such
as uniforms, bags, shoes,
and books, while chil-
dren are eagerly looking
forward to returning to
classrooms after the holi-
days.

Both government and
private schools are wit-
nessing heightened activ-
ity ahead of the reopen-
ing of schools on Friday.

According to official
statistics, Kurnool dis-
trict has emerged as the
top district in the state in
terms of student
strength, with a total of
2.55 lakh students. The
district had been given
the target of enrolling
25,000 new students this
year, of which nearly
18,000 admissions have
been completed so far,
which is 74 per cent of
the target.

“We have focused par-
ticularly on identifying
children from migrant
families and those in
anganwadi centres. We
have ensured their
admissions into nearby
schools,” said Kurnool
district education officer
(DEO) L. Srinivasulu.

Officials say despite
high migration trends in
Rayalaseema, Kurnool,
Nandyal, Kadapa, and
Anantapur districts have
performed well, crossing
the 70 per cent enrolment
mark. This achievement
is attributed to intensi-
fied awareness cam-
paigns, community

## Ronaldo goofs
up for Portugal

**Leiria (Portugal), June**
**11:** Portugal are heading
to the FIFA World Cup on
the back of a 2-1 warm-up
win over Nigeria and
some regrets for star
striker Cristiano
Ronaldo.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo
failed to add to his men's-
record international haul
of 143 goals despite being
presented with clear-cut
chances with just the
goalkeeper to beat in both
halves in Leiria on
Wednesday.

The five-time world
player of the year was
substituted off in the 65th
minute, having been
given longer on the field

than every other outfield
player to start the match
for Portugal.

Ronaldo will be making
his record-tying sixth
appearance at a World
Cup.

Francisco Conceicao,
one of the 11 replace-
ments to come on for
Portugal, grabbed the
75th-minute winner by
cutting in from the right
and curling a shot into
the far corner.

Pedro Neto gave
Portugal the lead in the
23rd. Akor Adams
equalised 14 minutes
later for Nigeria, which
had failed to qualify for
the World Cup. — AP

## Kylian, Neymar
top name game

**Quito (Ecuador), June**
**11: What's in a name? A**
victory foretold or a hom-
age to greatness past?

Across South America,
a legion of pint-sized
Kylians and Neymars will
be following the fortunes
of the stars to whom they
owe their names when the
World Cup kicks off.

But in a year's time,
depending on which play-
ers shine, expectant par-
ents may be leaning
towards Lamine (Yamal,
Spain), Ousmane
(Dembele, France), Harry
(Kane, England) or
Vitinha (Portugal).

In Ecuador, which is
taking part in its fifth
World Cup, the most pop-
ular footballers' names
are not those of local
stars such as Kendry Paez
or Willian Pacheco, a two-
time Champions League
winner with Paris Saint-
Germain.

Instead it is Brazil’s all-
time record scorer
Neymar, playing at his
fourth and probably last
World Cup, who tops the
board, with 3,847 name-
sakes, the country’s civil
registry said Wednesday.

Kylian Mbappe, the
wunderkind who led
France to victory at the
2018 World Cup in Russia,
is second, with over 2,800
children bearing his
name, ahead of James
(Rodriguez, Colombia's
captain), in third with
2,136 nods.

Portuguese greats Lionel
Messi and Cristiano
Ronaldo also have (their
first and last) names writ
large in Ecuadorian fami-
ly history.

The country boasts 1,549
little Lionels, 38 Messis,
178 Cristianos and 1,006
Ronaldo.

In Colombia, the order
is reversed, with 836 chil-
dren named Kylian or
Mbappe, ahead of 269
Neymars and 220
Cristianos or Ronaldo,
figures from 2022 show.

Neymar unsurprisingly,
has also inspired a gener-
ation of parents in his
homeland, with 2,443 chil-
dren named after the
player who has been an
integral part of three
World Cup campaigns,
according to a 2022 cen-
sus.

But Brazil also have a
soft spot for Kylian or
Killian, with over 400
bearing his name.

Argentine and

In football-mad
Argentina, Lionel had a
major moment in 2023,
the year after Messi
cemented his legacy by
leading his country to its
third title, but the name
has since dipped in popu-
larity.

In Chile, one family
made national headlines
in the run-up to the 2022
World Cup when it wel-
comed a newborn named
Griezmann Mbappe, after
France’s former striker
and current star forward
respectively. — AFP
